title: Symlink-safe scanning, shared agent skills, and folder-scoped rules
summary: The scan walker in `crates/osf` no longer follows symlinks: `collect_files` uses `symlink_metadata` and counts every link it refuses to walk into a new `skipped` tally, which `resolve_scan_targets` returns and `scan_paths` folds into the existing `excluded` count, so a tree of nothing but links reports "1 excluded" instead of a clean scan. Alongside that, the repository's agent guidance is reorganised: shared skills move to `.agents/skills` with `.claude/skills` as a git symlink, folder-specific rules move into per-folder `AGENTS.md` files, and CI gains two steps that lint every skill and assert the symlink mode is 120000.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: osf scan --config osf.toml <path>
nodes.summary: The command-line shell. It parses the scan invocation and prints the human or machine report; it holds no scanning logic of its own.

nodes.label: scan_paths
nodes.subtitle: pub fn scan_paths(dir, paths, rules, excluder)
nodes.summary: Reads each resolved target, skipping binaries and excluded labels, and now also skips any target that is itself a symlink. The skipped-link count seeds `dropped`, so links land in the same `excluded` total the report already prints.

nodes.label: resolve_scan_targets
nodes.subtitle: -> (Vec<(String, PathBuf)>, usize)
nodes.summary: Builds the label/path pairs to scan. With no paths it lists git-tracked files and reports zero skipped links; with explicit paths it walks them and returns how many symlinks the walk refused to follow.

nodes.label: collect_files
nodes.subtitle: symlink_metadata, never follows a link
nodes.summary: The recursive walker. It now stats with `symlink_metadata` and, on seeing a link, increments `skipped` and returns instead of descending. That single guard is what makes a self-referential link terminate and keeps a walk inside the folder it was given.

nodes.label: ScanOutcome
nodes.subtitle: files + excluded
nodes.summary: The result the CLI prints. Its `excluded` field now carries skipped symlinks as well as excluder matches, which is why a repo of only a link reports "1 excluded" rather than a clean scan.

nodes.label: git tracked files
nodes.subtitle: crate::git::tracked_files
nodes.summary: The default target list when no path is given. A tracked symlink appears here like any other entry, and is then filtered out by the symlink check in `scan_paths`.

nodes.label: .claude/skills
nodes.subtitle: git symlink -> ../.agents/skills
nodes.summary: A tracked symlink so Claude Code, which reads only `.claude/skills`, sees the same skills every other agent reads from `.agents/skills`. It is also the concrete case the new scan rule protects: a link is never read as the directory it points at.

nodes.label: .agents/skills
nodes.subtitle: shared agent skills
nodes.summary: The one home for skills an agent uses while working on this repository: adding-an-osf-command, filing-an-issue, opening-a-pull-request, reviewing-a-pull-request.

nodes.label: skills/
nodes.subtitle: show-me, pr-outline
nodes.summary: The skills the repository ships to adopters. Their closing credit lines moved out of `SKILL.md` into `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the folder READMEs, so a skill file holds only what an agent acts on.

nodes.label: ci.yml
nodes.subtitle: pull request gate
nodes.summary: The workflow that judges a pull request. Two steps were added to the existing job, both gated on the same change-detection output as the build.

nodes.label: Check the skills
nodes.subtitle: osf lint skill --format human
nodes.summary: Lists every `skills/*/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` directory via `git ls-files`, notices and exits when there are none, and otherwise runs the release `osf` binary over them.

nodes.label: Check the Claude Code skills link
nodes.subtitle: git ls-files -s .claude/skills
nodes.summary: Asserts git records `.claude/skills` with mode 120000 and that `readlink` resolves to `../.agents/skills`, failing with a Windows-specific fix hint otherwise. This is what keeps the symlink from silently becoming a plain file.

nodes.label: scan.rs tests
nodes.subtitle: 5 new symlink cases
nodes.summary: Covers a tracked link to a directory, a repo whose only entry is a dangling link, an explicit symlinked directory path, a link nested inside a scanned folder, and a link that cycles back on an ancestor.

nodes.label: TempRepo::symlink
nodes.subtitle: std::os::unix/windows::fs::symlink
nodes.summary: Test helper that creates a link relative to its own parent, creating parent directories first, and picks `symlink_dir` or `symlink_file` on Windows so a dangling target still works.

edges.label: scan
edges.summary: The scan command hands its paths and config to the engine.

edges.label: (targets, skipped_links)
edges.summary: The call now returns a skipped-link count alongside the targets, and that count seeds the excluded total.

edges.label: walk, never through a link
edges.summary: Each explicit path is walked with a mutable `skipped` counter; the walker bumps it and returns on any symlink rather than descending.

edges.label: tracked paths
edges.summary: With no explicit paths, the target list comes from git and no links are skipped at this stage.

edges.label: symlink_metadata per target
edges.summary: A tracked entry that is a symlink is now detected here and counted as excluded instead of being read.

edges.label: excluded = dropped + skipped
edges.summary: Skipped links and excluder matches share one counter, so the report never reads as a clean scan of nothing.

edges.label: after cargo build
edges.summary: Runs once per pull request that touches the workspace, over both skill folders.

edges.label: git ls-files -s, readlink
edges.summary: The check reads the recorded mode and the link target, and fails the job when either is wrong.

edges.label: ../.agents/skills
edges.summary: The link is the only path by which Claude Code reaches the shared skills.

flows.title: Scanning a tree that contains a symlink
flows.summary: What happens when `osf scan` is pointed at a folder holding a link, or at a link itself: the walker refuses to follow it, the count rises, and the report says something was skipped rather than reporting a clean scan.

messages.label: collect_files(path, out, &mut skipped)
messages.note: The walker now takes a skipped counter it can increment.

messages.label: symlink_metadata says link: skipped += 1, return
messages.note: This early return is what stops a link that cycles back on an ancestor from recursing forever.

messages.label: (targets, skipped_links)
messages.note: `dropped` starts at `skipped_links`, so links are already counted before any file is read.

messages.label: target is a symlink: dropped += 1, continue
messages.note: A second guard for targets that came from git rather than from the walk, so a tracked link is skipped too.

messages.label: ScanOutcome { files, excluded }
messages.note: A repo whose only tracked entry is a dangling link now reports "1 excluded" instead of a clean scan.
